key_insight: A hybrid control framework uses frequency-division multiplexing (FDM) to share microwave lines across superconducting qubits, targeting a 10–100× reduction in control-line count.
engineering_relevance: Shared control lines could ease dilution-refrigerator wiring and cooling constraints on the path to large-scale fault-tolerant quantum computing.
method: Combine polychromatic microwave pulses with band-pass filters to multiplex gate control.
Demonstrate parallel FDM-controlled CZ and XY(π/2) gates with 1:4 multiplexing.
Integrate the gate-control scheme with on-chip DC sources in a periodically extensible architecture.
evidence_signal: The 1:4 demonstration reports average parallel-gate errors of (6.4±0.2)×10⁻³ for CZ and (10.6±0.2)×10⁻⁴ for XY(π/2), with no statistically significant multiplexing-induced degradation.
watch_item: The projected 10–100× line reduction remains to be validated at scale, where frequency allocation, filter integration, and crosstalk may constrain performance.
paper_title: A Control Line Multiplexing Framework for Scalable Quantum Computing
